title: Entering a story or remainder now hands focus to the editor pane

stories.name: Entering a story or remainder focuses the editor
stories.premise: Two new scenarios pin that stepping into a Story or the unclaimed Remainder from the spine hands focus to the editor pane, and the two `update()` arms that start a walk each grow the one line that does it.

steps.name: Story-entry spec
steps.claim: A new scenario pins the missing behaviour: with the file tree focused, entering a Story from the spine must leave the editor pane focused.
steps.why: Before this scenario, `walking_a_story.feature` only asserted what the site mark and cursor did once a Story was entered — never which pane held focus. A reviewer who opens Story view from the tree and presses Enter on a row expects to land in the editor reading the code, not still sitting in the tree with nothing to press `n`/`p` against.

flow.in: The reviewer opens Story view with the file tree pane focused, then enters the Story "Keys reach the child".
flow.out: `then the editor pane has focus` — a new assertion the old `EnterStory` arm did not satisfy.

site.text:
Scenario: Entering a story from the spine focuses the editor
    Given I opened Story view
    And the file tree pane has focus
    When I enter the story "Keys reach the child"
    Then the editor pane has focus

steps.name: EnterStory focus
steps.claim: `Event::EnterStory` now sets `next.focus = Pane::Editor` alongside starting the walk, right where it already computes the step to open.
steps.why: `Pane` (`Tree`, `Editor`, `Terminal`, `Ai`) is the enum AGENTS.md asks for in place of a loose bool — one field the router already reads to decide where keys go, so setting it here is the whole fix; nothing downstream needs to know a Story was just entered versus focus being changed any other way.

flow.in: `Event::EnterStory(index)`, once the Story and its first Step have been found in the loaded `Artifact`.
flow.out: `next.focus = Pane::Editor` alongside the existing `Effect::OpenAt` that moves the cursor to the step's site.

steps.name: Remainder spec
steps.claim: The same gap is pinned for the Remainder: entering it from a focused file tree must also land focus on the editor.
steps.why: The Remainder is chosen from the spine and stepped through the same way a Story is (per the comment above `Event::EnterRemainder`), so the focus behaviour has to match — a reviewer walking a Remainder location has no reason to expect a different outcome than walking a Story.

flow.in: The reviewer opens Story view with the file tree focused, on a range with an unclaimed hunk in "src/mouse.rs", then enters the Remainder.

site.text:
Scenario: Entering the remainder from the spine focuses the editor
    Given "src/mouse.rs" has an unclaimed hunk
    And I opened Story view
    And the file tree pane has focus
    When I enter the remainder
    Then the editor pane has focus

steps.name: Remainder focus
steps.claim: `Event::EnterRemainder` grows the identical line, setting focus to the editor before returning the `OpenAt` effect for the first unclaimed location.
steps.why: Same fix, same shape, in the sibling arm — the Remainder has no Story or Step to load, only a bare location, so this line is the entire behavioural difference between the old and new handler.

flow.in: `Event::EnterRemainder`, once `story::remainder_locations` has produced at least one location.
flow.out: `next.focus = Pane::Editor` alongside the existing `Effect::OpenAt` for the first location.

stories.name: Two prior tickets marked done
stories.premise: The two tickets this focus fix rides alongside — Story titles/Step names, and the spine rendering the title — were already shipped in earlier commits, so this range closes them out in the tracker.

steps.name: Ticket 01 → done
steps.claim: Ticket 01, "Story sets and Steps require a name", flips from `ready-for-agent` to `done` — its `title`/`name` schema fields and refusal behaviour already shipped in commit c90a1c0.
steps.why: AGENTS.md's issue tracker records a `Status:` line per ticket rather than a separate progress checklist, so closing finished work means editing that line in place, not deleting the file.

steps.name: Ticket 02 → done
steps.claim: Ticket 02, "The spine shows the Story set's title", is closed the same way — the spine header and indented Story rows it specifies already shipped in commit 739a73e.
steps.why: Ticket 02 was blocked on ticket 01's `Artifact.title` field; both are now implemented and this range simply records that in the tracker.
